source.name: WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th edition (2021), with the ICCR integrated-diagnosis dataset

caseFields.label: Imaging / clinical
caseFields.placeholder: Ring-enhancing right frontal lesion with surrounding oedema

fields.label: Subtype
fields.help: Chordoid and clear cell carry CNS WHO grade 2. Papillary and rhabdoid no longer grade on the morphology alone; they take the grade the criteria give.

fields.label: Mitoses (per 1.6 mm², 10 high-power fields)
fields.help: 4 to 19 is grade 2, 20 or more is grade 3. The full 1.6 mm² must be examined; a count extrapolated from a smaller area cannot carry the grade.

fields.label: Atypical features
fields.help: Three or more of the five carry CNS WHO grade 2. Necrosis counts only when spontaneous; necrosis after embolisation or radiation does not.

fields.label: Frank anaplasia
fields.help: Overtly malignant cytology resembling carcinoma, high-grade sarcoma or melanoma. An independent CNS WHO grade 3 criterion.

fields.label: Brain invasion
fields.default: No adjacent brain in the specimen
options: No adjacent brain in the specimen
fields.help: Tumour through the leptomeninges into the subjacent parenchyma. Extension along Virchow-Robin spaces does not qualify; the pia is intact.

fields.label: Immunohistochemistry
options: H3 K27me3 loss of nuclear expression

fields.label: Mitoses (per 10 high-power fields)
fields.help: Counted in the most mitotically active area. Ten fields of 0.24 mm2 are 2.4 mm2, the area the glioma grading threshold is stated over; the meningioma threshold is stated over ten fields of 0.16 mm2. Both are read here as counts per ten high-power fields.

fields.label: Mismatch repair proteins
fields.help: MSH2, MSH6, MLH1 and PMS2. Considered under 18 with an H3-wildtype high-grade glioma, and at 18 to 40 where an H3- and IDH-wildtype high-grade glioma does not meet the glioblastoma criteria.

fields.label: p53 (immunohistochemistry)
options: Abnormal, overexpression in over 90% of nuclei

fields.label: Other higher-grade alterations
fields.help: Alterations that mark an IDH-mutant astrocytoma out as higher risk at the grade 2 / 3 interface. Any one of them carries the proposal to grade 3 where microvascular proliferation, necrosis, CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion and PDGFRA amplification are absent.

fields.label: BRAF fusion
fields.help: KIAA1549::BRAF is the commonest MAPK pathway alteration in pilocytic astrocytoma. It is also seen in pilomyxoid astrocytoma, ganglioglioma and diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumour, so it is read with the morphology rather than on its own.

fields.label: Other MAPK pathway alteration
fields.help: NF1, FGFR1, NTRK1/2/3, RAF1 and the rest, where they have been tested.

fields.label: Chromosome 7 / 10 (FISH)
options: Combined gain of chromosome 7 and loss of chromosome 10

fields.label: EZHIP (immunohistochemistry)
fields.help: Supports a posterior fossa group A ependymoma where H3 K27me3 staining is ambiguous and methylation profiling is unavailable.

fields.label: ZFTA fusion
fields.help: A ZFTA fusion with supratentorial localisation is the essential criterion for supratentorial ependymoma, ZFTA fusion-positive. RELA is the commonest partner; MAML2, MAML3, NCOA1, NCOA2, MN1 and CTNNA2 are also reported. Rare posterior fossa cases carry a ZFTA fusion and are designated NEC.

fields.label: YAP1 fusion
fields.help: A YAP1 fusion with supratentorial localisation is the essential criterion for supratentorial ependymoma, YAP1 fusion-positive. YAP1::MAMLD1 is typical, YAP1::FAM118B less so.

fields.label: MYCN amplification
fields.help: Amplification with spinal localisation is the essential criterion for spinal ependymoma, MYCN-amplified. Worth ordering where a spinal ependymoma is high grade or the radiology is aggressive, because high-grade histology is not always present. Diffuse midline glioma, H3 K27-altered can also be MYCN-amplified.

fields.label: Ependymal surrogate immunohistochemistry
fields.help: Surrogates for the compartment-specific molecular test where that test is unavailable. L1CAM with nuclear p65 supports a ZFTA fusion supratentorially; both negative points to YAP1 or to NEC. HOXB13 separates myxopapillary ependymoma from spinal ependymoma.

fields.label: Copy number (ependymal)
fields.help: Additional molecular information rather than type-defining. 1q gain and 6q loss carry a worse outcome in PFA; 22q loss supports spinal ependymoma; a stable genome fits PFA and aneuploidy fits PFB.

fields.label: Classifier and version
fields.placeholder: DKFZ / Heidelberg brain tumour classifier v12.8

fields.label: Calibrated score
fields.help: 0 to 1. A score below the laboratory threshold may still contribute where the other findings support the class; it cannot carry the class on its own.

fields.label: Immunohistochemistry
options: CD3 positive in scattered background T cells

fields.label: Fresh tissue sent for flow cytometry
Special stains
options: Luxol fast blue shows myelin loss with axonal preservation on neurofilament

snippets.label: Integrated diagnosis to follow
snippets.text: Molecular studies have been requested; the integrated diagnosis and CNS WHO grade will be issued in a supplementary report.

snippets.label: MGMT testing
snippets.text: MGMT promoter methylation testing has been requested; the result will be issued in a supplementary report.

snippets.label: Meningioma — molecular for grading
snippets.text: TERT promoter sequencing and CDKN2A/B copy-number analysis have been requested; the CNS WHO grade will be confirmed in a supplementary report.

snippets.label: Lymphoma — flow and staging
snippets.text: The diagnosis should be correlated with flow cytometry, cerebrospinal fluid examination and staging investigations.

snippets.label: Corticosteroid effect
snippets.text: Corticosteroid therapy before biopsy may obscure a lymphoid infiltrate; a repeat biopsy should be considered if the clinical and radiological picture is unchanged.

snippets.label: Scanty or crushed tissue
snippets.text: The tissue available is limited and a higher-grade component elsewhere in the lesion cannot be excluded; correlation with imaging is recommended.
